latex_table_note: All 12 pairs the pharmacist confirmed as contradictions, out of 299 annotated pairs (241 not a contradiction, 46 ambiguous). Rule is the generating rule that put the pair in the annotation pool: R1 same drug with opposite actions across the two notes, R2 two unequal sets of agents of one pharmacologic class, one continued and one ceased, R3 the same drug at doses differing by more than 20 percent, R4 a drug held in the nursing note and absent from the discharge summary. Rule counts are 3, 3, 4 and 2. Drug and class are dictionary terms: the normalised drug name is a member of the extraction dictionary and the class is a fixed hand-written class map of agents, not a standard terminology, so neither is note content. Danger is the pharmacist's ordinal rating, 1 the least and 5 the most clinically dangerous; the 12 ratings have median 2.5 and mean 2.9167, and 4 of 12 are at 4 or above. Conflict type is the coarse reading of the two sides; of the 3 class substitutions, 1 swaps the agent inside the class and 2 read as a class-level instruction set against the same agent, which the rule admits because it requires the two sides' agent sets to be unequal rather than disjoint, so they may overlap on one agent. Of the 4 dose rows, 3 carry a percent difference above 100 because a bolus figure is paired against a maintenance figure; those are unit and role mismatches in the parsed dose, not dose errors of that size. No clinical note text and no patient or admission identifier appears in this table.
